diagnostics.message: module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami:module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami_lambda: explicit depends_on of module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami:resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami_lambda: explicit depends_on of module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami:module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.ec2_update_runner_tags:module.ec2_update_runner_tags_lambda: explicit depends_on of module.ec2_update_runner_tags:resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ec2_update_runner_tags_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:module.runners: explicit depends_on of :data.external.download_lambdas is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`module.runners` has an explicit `depends_on = [data.external.download_lambdas]`, but the module already depends on that data source implicitly through its `webhook_lambda_zip`, `runner_binaries_syncer_lambda_zip` and `runners_lambda_zip` arguments (`${data.external.download_lambdas.result.path}/...`). The `depends_on` entry is redundant.

The lambda module already references the log group via `logging_log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami_lambda.name`, so the explicit `depends_on = [aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami_lambda]` duplicates an existing implicit dependency.

The event target already depends on the lambda module implicitly via `arn = module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami_lambda.lambda_function_arn`, so `depends_on = [module.ec2_update_runner_ssm_ami_lambda]` is redundant.

The lambda module already references the log group via `logging_log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ec2_update_runner_tags_lambda.name`, so the explicit `depends_on = [aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ec2_update_runner_tags_lambda]` duplicates an existing implicit dependency.

`data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami_id` reads `/github-action-runners/${var.runner_configs.prefix}/${key}/runners/config/ami_id`, but those parameters are created by `module.runners` (the multi-runner module's SSM runner-config parameters, enabled via `enable_ssm_on_runners = true`). Terraform sees no relationship between the two, so on a fresh apply the data source is read before the parameters exist and fails with ParameterNotFound. The data source should depend on `module.runners` (e.g. an explicit `depends_on`), since nothing about the parameter name can reference the module in a clean way.
